question: What is inertia?

options.text: The ability of an object to change its velocity
The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion
The force applied by an engine to move a vehicle
The force that pulls an object towards the Earth

solution:
The correct answer is __**The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Inertia** is a fundamental property of matter that describes the **tendency of an object to resist changes** to its state of motion or rest unless acted upon by an external force. 
• This concept is directly related to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, which states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. 
• Inertia is not a force but rather a property of mass. Objects with greater mass have **greater inertia**, meaning they resist changes in their state of motion more than objects with lesser mass.
